kind: one-shot synthetic pinned-source interleaving; no live allocation
hypothesis: A typed health event arriving immediately after the completion-drain qsize snapshot can remain queued while a previously queued terminal is processed, allowing current-main prepare_action_admission to evaluate the older latest observation and return READY.
test: Execute pinned drain helper, exact completion-time branch, actual prepare_action_admission, and actual final action-validity functions. Queue one completed verified-empty terminal before qsize; inject health 100→70 immediately after qsize returns its snapshot count. Observe whether final admission becomes READY before the late sample is delivered to the monitor.
decision: PASS_LATE_OBSERVATION_STALE_ADMISSION only if the late sample remains queued through production action-admission evaluation, the action becomes READY on the stale sample, and subsequent delivery of the late row produces hard invalidation. Otherwise record the actual fail-closed result.
counterhypothesis: The post-completion controller may necessarily consume or reject the late observation before fresh executor admission even when it arrives after the finite backlog snapshot.
limits: Synthetic scheduling establishes a possible ordering, not that the race occurs at a meaningful rate in live operation.
No executor action is submitted, and no input/game/GUI/OS behavior is measured.
No live threat exposure, HUD accuracy/cadence, real response time, recovery efficacy, progress, survival, or task outcome is measured.
retry_policy: Run candidate once after frozen-source preflight; preserve first output. Audit and mutation tests are read-only.
